feedback.overall:
1. Overall assessment  
Strong, credible CV for a senior digital communications role: the progression at NACo is clear, relevant, and shows increasing scope. Writing is polished and professional, but the document is somewhat repetitive and would be stronger with sharper outcomes, cleaner formatting, and a few language/style fixes.

1. Top strengths  
- Clear career progression within one organization, culminating in director and consultant roles, which supports credibility and leadership growth.  
- Strong alignment between headline, summary, skills, and experience; the CV consistently positions you as a digital strategy and communications leader.  
- Good use of scale indicators (10,000+ pages, 3.5 million page views, 50+ publishers), which adds impact and substance.

1. Top improvements  
- Add more measurable outcomes beyond scope metrics: include results such as engagement growth, efficiency gains, audience increases, cost savings, or campaign performance.  
- Reduce duplication across “Core Competencies,” “Topline Skills,” and “Technical + IT”; these sections overlap and make the CV feel longer than necessary.  
- Fix style/grammar consistency: use “12 years of experience” (not “12 years experience”); add serial commas consistently (“content operations, and enterprise web improvement”); standardize punctuation in bullets; and consider changing “Coleman DAVIS” to title case unless all-caps is intentional branding.
feedback.intro:
Quick assessment: Strong, credible intro that aligns well with the CV’s senior digital leadership focus. It would be stronger with tighter phrasing, one or two concrete signals of scale, and less repetition of skills already covered elsewhere.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Change “more than 12 years experience” to “12+ years of experience” and tighten the opening: “Digital communications and strategy leader with 12+ years of experience…”
- Add one concrete scope marker from recent roles, e.g., “leading enterprise web, email, social, and multimedia programs for a national membership organization.”
- Replace generic phrases like “expert in” with sharper value language: “drives cross-channel strategy, platform modernization, and editorial workflow design for complex, mission-driven organizations.”
- Consider revised version: “Digital communications and strategy leader with 12+ years of experience leading enterprise web, content, email, social media, and multimedia programs for mission-driven organizations. Brings deep expertise in cross-channel strategy, Drupal-based platform modernization, analytics, and editorial workflow design. Strong track record translating policy and technical issues into clear content, aligning stakeholders, and building systems that improve digital operations at scale.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-channel communications,” “platform modernization,” and “workflows/systems” repeat heavily in Core Competencies and Topline Skills.
- “Advocacy messaging” overlaps with multiple NACo role descriptions; keep the intro broader unless targeting advocacy-specific roles.
feedback.coreCompetencies:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant themes, but this block is broad and overlaps heavily with the header, Topline Skills, and Soft Skills. Tightening the phrasing and emphasizing higher-value leadership areas will make it more distinctive and senior.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Use parallel, noun-based phrasing and pluralize for consistency: “Multi-channel communications,” not “communication.”
- Prioritize strategic and leadership-oriented items over generic ones; e.g., move “Digital strategy & transformation,” “Editorial systems & governance,” and “Web platform modernization” earlier.
- Replace vague or overlapping terms with sharper language: “Workflow & systems architecture” → “Content operations & workflow architecture”; “Web & CMS administration” → “Web platform & CMS management.”
- Suggested rewrite: Digital strategy & transformation • Web platform modernization • Editorial systems & governance • Multi-channel communications • Content operations & workflow architecture • Analytics, reporting & optimization • Stakeholder & cross-functional leadership • Policy & advocacy communications • Multimedia & live event production

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Stakeholder & cross-department coordination” duplicates Soft Skills and the header.
- Several items overlap with Topline Skills; consider using this section for broader themes only, leaving tools/platforms to later sections.

items.title: Strategic Communications Consultant
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Consult a U.S.-based national membership organization on digital strategy, campaign platforms, content operations and enterprise web improvement.
- Build and refine digital systems, workflows and analytics that support coordinated organization-wide communications.
- Develop campaign and storytelling experiences within the organization’s Drupal platform, including custom microsite structures, modular content sections and downloadable member-facing toolkits.
- Deliver CMS development, front-end implementation and technical troubleshooting for large public-facing web properties.
- Advise on governance, usability and operational best practices across web, email, social and multimedia channels.
- Lead development of an AI-enabled search initiative, shaping retrieval strategy, structured content workflows and user-facing discovery design.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant current role, but it reads as a service list rather than a high-impact consulting entry. Tighten it around strategic outcomes and distinguish it from the earlier NACo staff roles.

Suggested edit:
- Open with scope + seniority: “Advise NACo on enterprise digital strategy, web modernization, and communications operations as an external consultant.”
- Consolidate overlapping bullets into 3–4 outcome-led bullets; e.g., combine digital systems/workflows/analytics/governance into one line.
- Emphasize distinctive current work: Drupal campaign builds, AI-enabled search, and cross-channel operating model improvements.
- Add measurable signals where possible: number of sites/campaigns launched, users supported, workflow efficiencies, search improvements, or stakeholder groups served.

Possible rewrite:
- Advise NACo on enterprise digital strategy, web modernization, and communications operations as an external consultant.
- Built Drupal-based campaign and storytelling experiences, including modular microsites, reusable content sections, and downloadable member toolkits.
- Improved cross-channel workflows, analytics, and governance to support coordinated web, email, social, and multimedia publishing.
- Led an AI-enabled search initiative spanning retrieval strategy, structured content design, and user-facing discovery.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Governance, workflows, analytics” overlaps heavily with Director of Digital Media; keep this entry focused on consulting-specific initiatives.
- Microsite and AI search details also appear in Recent Projects; avoid repeating the same phrasing verbatim.

items.title: Director of Digital Media
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led NACo’s digital communications team, overseeing the organization’s website, email, social media and video platforms, along with digital strategy, analytics, governance and budget management.
- Led the redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page website into a new Drupal platform supporting 3.5 million annual page views, 6,000+ average daily users and 50+ internal publishers.
- Directed NACo’s core digital communications channels, including email newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and social media platforms serving thousands of followers.
- Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house video studio, expanding in-house capacity for advocacy programming, event production and recurring multimedia content.
- Expanded the organization’s analytics infrastructure across GA4, Microsoft Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio and BigQuery, improving reporting and strategic decision-making.
- Strengthened digital operations through clearer governance, publishing standards and cross-department planning systems.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, high-impact leadership entry with good scale metrics. It should be tightened to emphasize outcomes and avoid repeating channel-management details already covered in adjacent NACo roles.

Suggested edit:
- Open with a sharper scope/result line: “Directed NACo’s digital media function across web, email, social, video, analytics, governance and budget management.”
- Rewrite bullets to foreground outcomes: “Led redesign and migration of a 10,000+ page Drupal website serving 3.5M annual page views, 6,000+ daily users and 50+ internal publishers.”
- Add measurable impact where missing, especially for email/social, video studio, and analytics (e.g., production cost savings, faster reporting, engagement growth, reduced vendor reliance, improved publishing consistency).
- Trim generic phrasing like “strengthened digital operations” and specify what changed: governance model, publishing standards, planning cadence, or cross-team workflow improvements.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Directed core digital communications channels” overlaps with the Associate Communications Director role; keep this entry focused on enterprise leadership and transformation.
- Video-program language may duplicate older NACo entries; emphasize building the in-house studio, not recurring production.

items.title: Associate Communications Director
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social media and video, helping scale NACo’s editorial coordination and advocacy communications.
- Managed four recurring weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.
- Produced and expanded a weekly advocacy video update, helping establish video as a recurring policy communications channel.
- Strengthened editorial planning and coordination across communications, advocacy and program teams.
- Helped improve the consistency and effectiveness of NACo’s digital publishing workflows.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression story, but this entry overlaps heavily with the adjacent NACo roles and reads more as support than leadership. Tighten it around what changed under your ownership and add any measurable growth or efficiency gains.

Suggested edit:
- Open with scope + outcome: “Led day-to-day digital communications operations across NACo’s web, email, social and video channels, improving editorial coordination and advocacy delivery.”
- Replace “helping” language with direct ownership: “Managed four weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.”
- Make the video bullet more outcome-focused: “Launched/grew a weekly advocacy video update into a recurring policy communications channel distributed across web, email and social.”
- Combine the last two bullets into one sharper line: “Built stronger cross-team editorial planning and standardized publishing workflows across communications, advocacy and program teams.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Weekly video updates” appears in the 2015–2018 role and the footer project list; differentiate this entry by emphasizing scale, formalization, or distribution.
- Website/email/social oversight is repeated in the 2022–2024 role; keep this entry focused on operational leadership and process improvements.

items.title: Digital Strategy & Content Leadership

- Editorial systems and governance

Suggested edit:
- Replace broad phrases with sharper, role-aligned wording: “Enterprise web strategy,” “Editorial governance and publishing operations,” “Cross-channel communications leadership,” “Public-sector advocacy communications,” “Audience-centered content strategy.”
- Consider adding one higher-value capability from recent work to increase specificity, e.g. “AI-enabled content discovery” or “Digital governance for multi-publisher environments.”

- Possible rewrite: “Enterprise web strategy • Editorial governance and publishing operations • Cross-channel communications leadership • Public-sector advocacy communications • Audience-centered content strategy”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Enterprise digital strategy” and “Editorial systems and governance” duplicate the header and Core Competencies almost verbatim.
- “Multi-channel communications leadership” also repeats Work Experience language; consider swapping in a more distinctive strength like “multi-publisher governance” or “AI-enabled content discovery.”

items.aiFeedback:

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from a long list to a sharper, impact-oriented summary:  
  **Drupal and CMS modernization • Front-end implementation (HTML, CSS, JavaScript, jQuery) • API integrations and workflow automation • Airtable-based content systems • AI-enabled search and discovery experiences**
- Prioritize Drupal first; it is the clearest recent platform strength from NACo work. Consider dropping WordPress/SharePoint/Power Pages here unless they are central to target roles.

- If space allows, use “search and discovery” instead of “search experiences” for a stronger product/UX signal.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- WordPress, SharePoint, Power Pages, Airtable, API integrations, and coding languages are already listed in “Technical + IT.”
- “CMS modernization” and “AI-enabled search experiences” also echo Core Competencies and recent project content.

items.title: University of Virginia

items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: The current line adds little value and reads like generic school marketing. For an experienced candidate, this education entry should be minimal and factual unless you have honors or distinctions worth adding.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the content line entirely with no body text; the degree, school, location, and dates are sufficient.
- If applicable, swap in a concrete credential instead: “Relevant coursework: …” or “Honors: …” only if genuinely strong and still relevant.
- Tighten the subtitle to “B.A., Economics and History” for cleaner formatting.
- Consider dropping dates if you want to reduce age signaling and keep focus on recent senior experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Ranked among the top public universities…” is generic and not candidate-specific, so it weakens the entry rather than strengthening it.
- Avoid adding coursework unless it clearly supports current digital strategy/communications work; otherwise it will feel disconnected from the stronger recent experience.

items.title: Web Platforms & CMS
items.content: Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid, relevant platform list, but it reads as a generic inventory and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” in Topline Skills. This item should either add specificity or be tightened to avoid repetition.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe to show level/relevance: “Drupal (enterprise migrations, modular content architecture) • WordPress • SharePoint • Microsoft Power Pages • GitHub Pages”
- If space allows, prioritize strongest/recent platform first and consider dropping the least material one: “Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages”
- Standardize naming for polish: use “Microsoft Power Pages” instead of “Power Pages”
- If you want more impact, add version/scope only where credible and recent, e.g., “Drupal 10”

- This largely duplicates Topline Skills [2], which already lists the same platforms plus broader web capabilities.
- “GitHub Pages” may feel lightweight versus the enterprise/public-sector emphasis unless supported elsewhere in experience/projects.

items.title: Coding & Technical Implementation
items.content: HTML5 • CSS3 • JavaScript • jQuery • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid technical coverage, but this item reads like a generic keyword list and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution.” Tighten it to emphasize implementation tools you actively use and modernize the phrasing.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Front-End Development & Technical Implementation**
- Rewrite as: **HTML/CSS • JavaScript (incl. jQuery) • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions**
- Use simpler labels unless version specificity matters elsewhere: change **HTML5/CSS3** to **HTML/CSS**
- If accurate, add one proof point in a nearby project/role bullet rather than here, e.g. “built custom front-end components,” “deployed edge scripts via Cloudflare Workers,” or “automated deployments with GitHub Actions”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- **JavaScript, jQuery, and API integrations** already appear in Topline Skills; keep them in one place or vary the framing
- This item risks overlap with **Web Platforms & Technical Execution**; use that section for broader capability and this one for hands-on tools only

items.title: Automation & Workflow Systems
items.content: Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Basecamp • Slack • Teams • Trello
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid tool coverage, but this item is too broad and mixes automation platforms with project/collaboration tools. It also overlaps with “Workflow automation and platform integration” in Core Competencies and “Airtable systems / Workflow automation” in Topline Skills.

Suggested edit:
- Split by function and tighten to the most relevant tools: “Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana” is stronger than listing every collaboration app.
- Rename for precision: “Automation, Workflow & Project Systems” or “Workflow Automation & Coordination Tools.”
- If these tools were used materially in recent roles, add a light qualifier: “Airtable, Power Automate, Zapier (workflow automation); Jira, Asana (project coordination).”
- Drop lower-signal/general workplace tools unless central to delivery: Slack, Teams, Trello, Basecamp.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Airtable” and “workflow automation” already appear in Topline Skills; avoid repeating both prominently.
- Slack/Teams are generic and don’t add much given the stronger systems/platform story elsewhere.

items.title: Email & Engagement Systems
items.content: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is relevant, but it reads as a bare vendor list and undersells your email/platform leadership. Because email operations already appear in recent NACo roles, this should stay concise and tool-focused rather than repeating channel ownership.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Email Marketing & Engagement Platforms**
- Tighten and standardize product names: **Dynamics 365 Customer Insights – Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp**
- If accurate, add scope via a light qualifier instead of a claim-heavy bullet, e.g.: **Enterprise email automation, newsletter distribution and audience engagement platforms**
- Keep the newest/most enterprise-grade platform first (Dynamics 365), with legacy/lighter tools after it.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Avoid adding outcomes like newsletter reach or email leadership here; those are already covered in recent Work Experience.
- If Higher Logic was the primary NACo platform, consider ordering it first instead of Dynamics 365 to better match demonstrated experience.

items.title: Work Eligibility
items.content: Full legal authorization to work in Belgium (Visa D + residence permit / carte de séjour)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful for Belgium-based applications, but the phrasing is a bit legalistic and takes more space than needed. This should read as a clear status note, not a headline achievement.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite for brevity and recruiter scanability: “Authorized to work in Belgium (Visa D and residence permit).”
- If accurate, make it stronger and simpler: “Fully authorized to work in Belgium; residence permit in place.”
- Avoid the French term unless the role specifically requires bilingual administrative terminology; “residence permit” is usually enough.
- Consider moving this into the contact/header area for local applications, since eligibility matters more there than in a secondary rail.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- No major duplication, but this item is lower-value than recent experience; keep it very short so it doesn’t compete for attention.
- If location/contact already signals Belgium and applications are local, this may be optional rather than essential.

items.title: Languages
items.content:
**English** (Native)
**French** (A2/Learning)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too compressed and visually awkward. It should be reformatted for quick scanning and framed honestly so French supports your Belgium-based role without overstating proficiency.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite as a simple line: Languages: English (native) | French (A2, currently improving)
- Use lowercase proficiency style for consistency and cleaner tone: native, A2, conversational/basic if accurate.
- If relevant to target roles, add practical context only if true: French (A2, professional working improvement underway)
- Keep it concise; this section is supporting information, not a selling point versus your recent digital leadership experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- No major duplication, but avoid overdesign/bolding here; the CV already has strong skills sections competing for attention.
- If space is tight, this can stay in the rail and should not be repeated in the header, summary, or cover letter unless language is job-relevant.

items.title: Soft Skills
items.content: Cross-department coordination • Stakeholder communication • Team leadership • Strategic planning • Clear writing and editing • Problem-solving • Adaptability
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This section is too generic and largely repeats strengths already proven in the summary and core competencies. On a senior CV, “soft skills” should either be removed or reframed as leadership traits tied to scope and outcomes.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to “Leadership Strengths” or “Management & Collaboration” to sound more senior and less filler.
- Cut generic items like “Problem-solving” and “Adaptability”; keep only traits that support target roles.
- Tighten to 4–5 items max, e.g.: Cross-functional leadership • Executive stakeholder management • Editorial judgment • Team development • Strategic planning
- If space is tight, remove this section entirely and use the room for quantified achievements in recent roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-department coordination” and “Stakeholder communication” duplicate the header summary and Core Competencies.
- “Team leadership” and “Strategic planning” are already demonstrated more credibly in the 2022–2024 Director role.

items.title: References
items.content: References available upon request.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item adds little value and uses space that could better support recent, higher-impact experience. “References available upon request” is assumed by most employers and usually should be removed.

Suggested edit:
- Delete the “References” entry entirely.
- Use the freed space for stronger supporting content instead, such as a brief “Selected Results” rail item with 1–2 metrics from recent roles.
- If references are specifically requested, provide them separately rather than on the CV.
- If you want a replacement rail item, consider “Work Authorization” or “Languages,” which are more useful and already present here.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section is redundant because reference availability is standard and does not differentiate you.
- Keeping it may weaken the second-page rail by displacing more relevant, recent qualifications.

items.title: Digital Media Manager / Producer
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Advanced through two digital roles, supporting the creation of the organization’s first in-house digital team and strengthening workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia. Contributed to a major website refresh and produced high-impact digital content—including livestreams and weekly video updates—while providing day-to-day guidance to a digital media associate.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression signal, but the item is still broad and overlaps with later NACo roles. Make it more foundational and execution-focused, with concrete outputs and team-building impact.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite to emphasize early-stage buildout: “Promoted across two digital roles to help establish NACo’s first in-house digital team and formalize workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia.”
- Add clearer ownership and outputs: “Supported a major website refresh; produced livestreams and a recurring weekly video update; coordinated day-to-day digital publishing and multimedia delivery.”
- Tighten management phrasing: replace “providing day-to-day guidance” with “mentored a digital media associate” or “supervised one digital media associate,” if accurate.
- Add metrics if available: number of livestreams/videos produced, audience growth, publishing volume, or efficiency gains from workflow improvements.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “weekly video updates” overlaps with the 2018–2022 role; frame this item as launching or piloting the format.
- “strengthening workflows” repeats later governance/operations themes; keep this at a lighter, foundational level.

items.title: County Solutions & Innovations Coordinator
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Coordinated innovation and research projects supporting organizational programs and policy work. Contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials, and launched the organization’s first podcast, overseeing planning, scripting, and production.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid early-career entry with a credible “first podcast” achievement, but it reads generically and overlaps with later NACo digital/media roles. Emphasize the distinct innovation/research scope and make the podcast launch the clearest outcome.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite to foreground scope and initiative: “Coordinated county innovation and research projects that supported NACo program development and policy communications.”
- Tighten the media portion: “Produced digital and multimedia content for organizational initiatives, including planning and creating supporting materials for program and policy campaigns.”
- Make the standout achievement sharper: “Launched NACo’s first podcast, leading concept development, episode planning, scripting and production.”
- If possible, add one measurable detail: number of projects supported, episodes produced, stakeholders served, or audience/download growth.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Avoid broad phrases like “digital content production and multimedia materials,” which are already covered more strongly in later digital media roles.
- Don’t overstate team leadership here; later entries better establish management and enterprise-scale ownership.
